question_text:
A clinical study is studying new genetic gene-based therapies for children and adults with sickle cell disease. The patients were informed that they were divided into two age groups since younger patients suffer from different complications of the disease. The pediatric group is more likely to suffer from which of the complications?
I. Splenic sequestration
II. Avascular necrosis
III. Pulmonary hypertension
IV. Acute chest syndrome
V. Nephropathy?

                    ### Question
                    A clinical study is studying new genetic gene-based therapies for children and adults with sickle cell disease. The patients were informed that they were divided into two age groups since younger patients suffer from different complications of the disease. The pediatric group is more likely to suffer from which of the complications?
I. Splenic sequestration
II. Avascular necrosis
III. Pulmonary hypertension
IV. Acute chest syndrome
V. Nephropathy?

                    ### Options
                    opa. I, II
opb. I, IV, V
opc. I, II, IV
opd. III, IV
ope. I, IV

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Pediatric patients with sickle cell disease are more likely to experience splenic sequestration and acute chest syndrome due to their age-related physiological characteristics. Splenic sequestration occurs more frequently in children because their spleens are often larger and more functional, making them susceptible to vaso-occlusive events. Acute chest syndrome is also more common in younger patients, often triggered by infections and vaso-occlusive crises. In contrast, complications such as avascular necrosis and nephropathy are more prevalent in older patients due to cumulative damage and chronic complications associated with sickle cell disease. Therefore, the pediatric group is primarily at risk for complications I (Splenic sequestration) and IV (Acute chest syndrome). This aligns with the consensus that younger patients face distinct complications compared to adults.
